reliability.rationale: The flexible probability reference achieves Brier0.14336 versus0.18844 expected utility on12 held participants. Compact context/history candidates improve utility but do not beat the flexible reference.

mechanism.rationale: Source authors already report context/age effects. Experimenter probabilities may be unknown to participants; correlated lag/history coefficients and incomplete coding documentation do not identify a unique cognitive mechanism.

novelty.rationale: Source-publication review is disclosed, but the model families are established and the search is targeted. No literature-priority certification.

significance.rationale: Useful matched-information probability benchmark with proper scoring, group calibration and event diagnostics; no demographic ranking or individual risk-trait claim follows.

reproducibility.rationale: Executable coefficients, native anchors and group evidence are present; independent computational review checks arithmetic separately.

impact.rationale: No independent clinical, industrial, financial or experimental intervention benefit was measured.

Separated calibrated prediction, mechanistic interpretation and novelty/impact claims
